Expands Aniah's Law so judges may deny bail to people charged with shooting into an occupied dwelling, building, vehicle or watercraft, or with solicitation, attempt or conspiracy to commit murder.
races.title: Deny bail for shootings into occupied places and murder plots

races.note: Bars reducing an elected district attorney's compensation during the term of office, matching the protection judges have.
races.title: No cutting district attorney pay during a term

races.note: Restores limits on contributions to state candidates, $2,000 per election from individuals and $4,000 from groups, adjusted for inflation every 10 years, after a 2021 court ruling voided the old limits.
races.title: Restore campaign contribution limits

races.note: Would have replaced the nominating commission and governor appointment with statewide partisan elections and six year terms for Kansas Supreme Court justices.
races.title: Elect Kansas Supreme Court justices

races.note: Lets the Legislature add or remove officers, positions and employees from the unclassified state civil service.
races.title: Legislature can move jobs in or out of unclassified civil service

races.note: Treats the St. George Community School System in East Baton Rouge Parish like a parish for school funding and operations.
races.title: St. George school system gets parish level school powers

races.note: Repeals certain constitutional education funds and uses their money plus Teachers' Retirement System savings for a $2,250 teacher raise and $1,125 support staff raise.
races.title: Repeal education funds to pay teacher and staff raises

races.note: Lets parishes reduce or exempt property tax on business inventory and provides for classifying public service property.
races.title: Let parishes exempt business inventory from property tax

races.note: Raises mandatory judicial retirement age from 70 to 75 and lets a judge finish a term in progress.
races.title: Raise judicial retirement age to 75

races.note: Continues the one tenth of one percent sales and use tax for state parks, historic sites and soil and water conservation for 10 more years.
races.title: Renew 0.1 percent parks and soil conservation sales tax

races.note: Removes the exemption that let Jackson County appoint its assessor, so all charter counties must elect an assessor who meets state training rules.
races.title: Require an elected Jackson County assessor

races.note: Would have required citizen initiated constitutional amendments to win a majority in each of the 8 congressional districts, banned foreign money in ballot campaigns and added petition fraud penalties.
races.title: Require initiative amendments to win every congressional district

races.note: Would have required the individual income tax to be cut with revenue growth until eliminated and allowed sales taxes on more goods and services.
races.title: Phase out state income tax and allow broader sales taxes

races.note: Requires citizen initiated and legislatively referred constitutional amendments to cover only one subject and bars the Secretary of State from approving multi subject petitions.
races.title: Single subject rule for constitutional amendments

races.note: Would have raised the state minimum wage from $7.25 to $12 in 2027, $13.50 in 2028 and $15 in 2029, then indexed it to inflation, and removed several exemptions.
races.title: Raise minimum wage to $15 by 2029

races.note: Would have let the Legislature set how the state reimburses local governments for revenue lost to property tax exemptions.
races.title: Legislature sets tax exemption reimbursement method

races.note: Adds proof of identity for every method of voting, including mail, to the Oklahoma Constitution, leaving the Legislature to define acceptable ID.
races.title: Put voter ID requirement in state constitution

races.note: Yes would have kept parts of HB 3991, raising the gas tax 6 cents a gallon, vehicle registration and title fees, and the transit payroll tax to 0.2 percent.
races.title: Uphold gas tax, payroll tax and vehicle fee increases

races.note: Lets the General Assembly temporarily adopt new congressional districts for 2026 through 2030 in response to other states' mid decade redistricting.
races.title: Allow mid decade congressional redistricting
